course_description:
Advanced concepts and practices used in the sustainable management of agriculture and animal systems in Australia. Students should contact agriculture@enquire.uq.edu.au to request permission to enrol into this course. Evidence of immunity to Q fever is mandatory for this course. Refer to UQ Student Immunisation Requirements for more information.

Students must contact agriculture@enquire.uq.edu.au to request permission to enrol into this course.

This course was last offered in external mode in 2025. Please contact the School if you have any questions regarding the external mode.

This is a capstone course, required to be completed in your final semester 2 of study, and as such we expect that students will interact with teaching staff and other students. You are a diverse cohort that brings together all majors offered within the Bachelor of Agricultural Science, this includes students across the Agronomy, Horticulture and Animal Science Programs and also students enrolled in the B.Ag.Sci/B.Ag.Bus dual degree.

In this course you will study concepts of sustainability as it relates to agricultural systems, encompassing soils, plants and animals, as well as components of the supply chain. We will also cover aspects of economic, environmental and social sustainability relevant to agricultural production in Australia and globally. Much of what we discuss will be aimed at best practice - but we do not assume that what we present is the only way that it can be done. This course has a focus on exposing you to sustainability pathways as they currently exist in production systems and future opportunities that may exist. We expect that you will read widely, attend lectures and question the content that is provided to you.

There are a number of internal and external (industry) guest lecturers that deliver content into this course, as such at times there may be a need to have late changes to the scheduled lecture series. Please ensure that you are monitoring Blackboard for the most up-to-date information.

This course has a compulsory field trip element . Attendance for the field trip element of this course can be achieved by one of two streams, as described below. Additional information about participating in Stream 1 and Steam 2 have been provided. You will need to nominate which field trip stream you are attending by Friday 31 July 2026, via the forms provided to you via Blackboard. Attendance on one of these field trip streams is compulsory to be eligible to pass the course.

Stream 1 -ﾠattend a series of day trips throughout semester as per the semester plan. We are still working with our industry partners to confirm our site visits. This information will be provided to you as soon as possible. Please be aware that locations may need to change as weather events can impede accessibility at some locations. All correspondence will be provided on Blackboard.

Stream 2 ﾠ- attend a 6-day field tour travelling across South-East and Central Queensland during week 9 of Semester (Sunday 20 - Friday 25 September 2026, inclusive). Students participating in Stream 2 will be required to pay up to $400 into a university account to support meal and accommodation costs during the tour. Apart from the meals covered by your $400 - you will need to cover the cost of all other meals, at most this will consist of 4 breakfasts, 3 lunches and 5 dinners. We will confirm what meals are covered during a Stream 2 information session.

We will be away for a total of 5 nights, our accommodation will be a mix of caravan park cabins and/or motel rooms, and tents (Goondicum Station). Rooms and tents are on a shared basis. Travel will be provided by a bus with a professional driver. Private vehicles are not allowed.

For both Stream 1 and Stream 2

This course hasﾠ mandatory immunisation requirements ﾠdue to an increased risk of Vaccine Preventable Diseases (VPD) for students working with animals or in agricultural environments. Students will be asked to provide evidence of immunity to Q fever via my.UQ My Requests as a condition of enrolment in this course. Refer to UQ Student Immunisation Requirements for more information.

For all field trips and practicals you are required to wear:

Mobile phones are not to be used during practicals/field trips and when on-site visits. Always ask permission before taking pictures.

Please note, that besides undertaking one of the two field trip streams, all students should attend four of the weekly practical sessions, with further details on exact dates to be provided in Blackboard. These practicals are associated with Assessment 2 and Assessment 3, and entail learning how to develop a Business Pitch and Business Case, visiting the participating businesses that are the focus of the activity, and presenting draft and final business pitches.

Due to the dynamic nature of this course, it is imperative that you regularly consult with Blackboard to ensure that you have the most up-to-date information.

At the School of Agriculture and Food Sustainability, we are committed to creating an inclusive and empowering learning environment for all students. We value and respect the diverse range of experiences our students bring to their education, and we believe that this diversity is crucial for fostering a rich culture of knowledge-sharing and meaningful exploration. We hold students and staff accountable for actively contributing to establishing a respectful and supportive learning environment.

Bullying, harassment, and discrimination in any form are strictly against our principles and against UQ Policy, and will not be tolerated. If you have any concerns about your experience in this course, we encourage you to tell a member of the course teaching team. Your well-being and a positive learning atmosphere are of utmost importance to us.

course_aims: Advanced concepts and practices used to ensure that agricultural and livestock production systems in Australia are sustainable.

learning_outcomes.description: Critically evaluate and integrate environmental, economic, and social dimensions of sustainability in agricultural systems.
Analyse and interpret production and system-level data to assess enterprise sustainability.
Diagnose, prioritise, and develop evidence-based strategies to address sustainability challenges and opportunities.
Work collaboratively to validate, communicate, and defend evidence-based solutions to agricultural sustainability challenges to diverse stakeholders.

assessment_details.task_description: Task Summary Size – Estimated 2000 – 3000 words (combined total). NOTE: Word count is not limited, this task is a reflection activity and needs to cover what it needs to cover. Presentation – typed, with a cover page. Background In this task you will need to provide your own personal reflections on each enterprise you attend, regardless of your involvement in Stream 1 or Stream 2 of the compulsory field work. You are expected to attend all sessions and write a reflection for each. If students miss an enterprise reflection, they will be awarded 0 marks for that specific reflection. Please note, these activities are not repeatable, there will be no alternative assessment for these enterprises. Reflection Structure For each of the enterprises visited, consider the following questions: 1. Enterprise description: Name, Location, Production enterprise description (i.e. what does this enterprise do?). 2. Does the enterprise have sustainability goals? If yes, what are they? If no, do opportunities exist? 3. What did you learn at this enterprise that you didn’t know before visiting? What was it? 4. Was there anything unexpected that you learned at this enterprise? 5. Would you recommend this location to friends/colleagues/peers to visit? Why? General Formatting and Communication Task Size – 200-300 words per reflection (excluding references, if used) What this means is that you are to address the five (5) questions above, where question one (1) does not count towards the word count. This means that your reflection across the whole semester will be about 2000 – 3000 words in total. General Formatting Your report must be typed, 1.5 to 2.0 line spacings are ok, font size 12, in Australian (British) English and neatly presented. Communicating your thoughts in a concise and grammatically correct manner is essential to any written document, here at The University of Queensland or outside this institution. One way to check is to read your assignment aloud to yourself, if it is awkward to speak then it is awkward to read. Acknowledging and/or referencing AI use This task is designed to be reflective of your personal experiences with our industry partners. It is envisaged that the use of AI will not be required. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. The use of AI or MT must be referenced appropriately. Please see assessment guidelines in blackboard course site for specific instructions. Students may also refer to Library guides found under Additional assessment information > Acknowledging and referencing AI use. To obtain a mark for the practical/field trip session students must participate and complete the associated exercises (submitting the reflections via Blackboard - Turnitin). If you do not participate in a practical/field trip class, or do not provide evidence of your attendance (i.e. signing attendance sheet, or scanning student ID), your reflection will not be marked/graded. Refer to late submission notes for more information. Absence from a Practical/Field Trip Session If you are unable to complete your timetabled practical/field trip session because of circumstances beyond your control (e.g., illness) you must submit a practical absence request immediately accompanied by acceptable supporting documentation. A list of acceptable reasons and required supporting documentation is found at https://my.uq.edu.au/information-and-services/manage-my-program/exams-and-assessment/applying-assessment-extension?p=1#1 Your request must be submitted no later than 24 hours following the missed practical/field trip/tutorial. The submission link can be found in the Learning Resources (Blackboard Original) or Course Resources (Blackboard Ultra) folder in your course Blackboard site. Requests without the correct supporting documentation may not be approved. If the reason for your absence is not approved, you will be considered as absent from that session and you will not be eligible for marks from that exercise. This course is unable to provide alternative practical sessions/ field trips to attend. If you do not complete the relevant practical session, you will be unable to complete the associated assessment item. If you require further assistance, please do not hesitate to contact the School - agriculture@enquire.uq.edu.au . Read full task description Hide full task description

You must submit your Assessment task, in Blackboard, via the Turnitin link by the submission deadline. You should also retain an electronic copy of every piece of assessment you submit.

You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
Submission of an Extension of Assessment Due Date (EADD) should be completed online through your My Requests tab via my.UQ Dashboard , in accordance with the University's Assessment Procedure (located in the Policies and Procedures section of this course profile) which outlines the requirements for requesting extensions to assessment due dates. Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
For example, a report worth a maximum of 40 marks, submitted 28 hours late will incur a penalty of 8 marks. This is calculated as 2 (24 hour periods) x 10% per period x 40 marks, resulting in 8 marks deducted from the student’s mark for the assessment.
Assessment deadlines are firm and must be met. Late submission without permission or non-submission of assessable work will result in penalties being applied . Late submission of assessment will only be granted for documented medical reasons, accident, bereavement, jury service and other circumstances allowed in the UQ Policies and Procedures Library (PPL).

assessment_details.task_description: Sustainable Innovation Pitch Background This assignment challenges students to develop and deliver a compelling pitch to present an idea to an industry partner on sustainable business innovations. The goal is to present a scenario for a sustainable business opportunity to our industry partner, drawing on your experience gained by visiting industry enterprises. As this activity is being undertaken in collaboration with a commercial partner, the activities associated with this Pitch are not repeatable, as such we are unable to provide any alternative assessment opportunities. Task In small groups of 4 to 5 members, you are required to prepare and deliver a professional pitch presentation, live in class - all students must attend in person. Your pitch will be 5 min with 2-3 min of question time. Your pitch should clearly communicate your sustainable business opportunity proposition, and the potential impact or value of your idea. Groups should be formed by the end of the Week 3 practical with a list of members provided to the course coordinator. If you are having trouble finding a group talk to the Course Coordinator. You must submit a copy of your PowerPoint slides (as a .pdf) to Blackboard, link provided by the submission deadline. One person per group will submit the Powerpoint slides, group members names and student numbers must be clearly identified on the introductory slide. More details will be provided in class and uploaded in Blackboard. The slides must be uploaded to blackboard by 2:00 pm Monday 26 October 2026. The exact date and time of the Pitch presentations will be announced in class and via a Blackboard announcement. This assessment will be marked by both teaching staff and industry collaborators. This assessment item is not eligible for a re-mark as it has been independently marked by two examiners and has undergone the prescribed moderation and review processes. As a result, there is no further academic judgement to be reconsidered through a re-mark process. assessment_details.task_description: Task In your Innovation Pitch groups, you are required to develop a 5-page business case pitch report to support your Sustainable Innovation Pitch - Presentation. This report should demonstrate your ability to identify a market opportunity, develop a viable business model, and communicate the value proposition effectively. Due to the connection with your Sustainable Innovation Pitch - Presentation, the activities associated with this Pitch - Business Case are not repeatable as this has been developed in collaboration with a commercial partner, as such we are unable to provide any alternative assessment opportunities. One person per group will submit the business case, group members names and student numbers must be clearly identified on the coversheet. Your business case pitch report must include the following sections: 1. Executive Summary (Approx. ½ page) This section will provide a brief overview of the sustainable business innovation and highlight the opportunity, sustainability, and expected outcomes. 2. Opportunity (Approx. 1 page) This section should describe and justify the opportunity with data or trends. 3. Business Solution (Approx. 1 page) Describe your product or service, highlight any unique aspects and describe how this opportunity will be sustainable. 4. Market Analysis (Approx. 1 page) How does this fit into the business from an industry and market approach? 5. Business Model & Strategy (Approx. 1 page) Outline a potential revenue model and pricing strategy. 6. Financial Snapshot (Approx. ½ page) Provide an overview of financial projections (e.g., start-up costs, revenue forecast, break-even). Describe any potential capital expenses. A more detailed assessment description and rubric will be made available via Blackboard. A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
For example, a report worth a maximum of 40 marks, submitted 28 hours late will incur a penalty of 8 marks. This is calculated as 2 (24 hour periods) x 10% per period x 40 marks, resulting in 8 marks deducted from the student’s mark for the assessment.
Assessment deadlines are firm and must be met. Late submission without permission or non-submission of assessable work will result in penalties being applied . Late submission of assessment will only be granted for documented medical reasons, accident, bereavement, jury service and other circumstances allowed in the UQ Policies and Procedures Library (PPL).

Task In your Innovation Pitch groups, you are required to develop a 5-page business case pitch report to support your Sustainable Innovation Pitch - Presentation. This report should demonstrate your ability to identify a market opportunity, develop a viable business model, and communicate the value proposition effectively. Due to the connection with your Sustainable Innovation Pitch - Presentation, the activities associated with this Pitch - Business Case are not repeatable as this has been developed in collaboration with a commercial partner, as such we are unable to provide any alternative assessment opportunities. One person per group will submit the business case, group members names and student numbers must be clearly identified on the coversheet. Your business case pitch report must include the following sections: 1. Executive Summary (Approx. ½ page) This section will provide a brief overview of the sustainable business innovation and highlight the opportunity, sustainability, and expected outcomes. 2. Opportunity (Approx. 1 page) This section should describe and justify the opportunity with data or trends. 3. Business Solution (Approx. 1 page) Describe your product or service, highlight any unique aspects and describe how this opportunity will be sustainable. 4. Market Analysis (Approx. 1 page) How does this fit into the business from an industry and market approach? 5. Business Model & Strategy (Approx. 1 page) Outline a potential revenue model and pricing strategy. 6. Financial Snapshot (Approx. ½ page) Provide an overview of financial projections (e.g., start-up costs, revenue forecast, break-even). Describe any potential capital expenses. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13 (27 Jul - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Lecture Series Lectures will cover a broad array of topics that discuss: sustainability issues and challenges across agriculture, technology usage for sustainability, productivity and stewardship, managing environments, and conflict or contentious plant species as they apply across all agricultural industries.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13 (27 Jul - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Industry Exposure During these sessions we will be exposing you to a range of sustainability related practices across crop and livestock industries. For Stream 1 participants you can expect to visit 6 to 7 sites during the semester, such as: plant nurseries, feedlot, abattoir and specialist crops. For Stream 2 participants you can expect to visit 10 to 12 sites during your six day trip, sites such as: grazing beef enterprises, organic beef, broadacre cropping, piggery, pecans and citrus.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13 (27 Jul - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Practical There are four sessions associated with developing a business pitch and business case (on a new and sustainable business opportunity) for an industry partner (either Camm Agriculture or Mort & Co.). In Week 2, representatives from these companies will provide you with an overview of their business. You will then do some activities around creating business pitches and business cases. In Week 3, you will go on an all-day trip to visit Wonga Plains feedlot (Camm Agriculture) and Grassdale (Mort & Co) that are located on the Darling Downs. In Week 7, we will have a practice session where you will present your draft business pitches in preparation for your final business pitches to both Camm Agriculture and Mort & Co. representatives, which will be held in week 13.
